_note: Resident personal income-tax bands. bands = [[from, rate%], ...] in local currency. Maintained by hand from the cited sources; re-check yearly.

Fiji.nonresident: 20% from the first dollar, same rates above FJD 270k
Fiji.capital_gains: 10% on disposal of capital assets incl. land/buildings and shares; residents also on foreign assets (credit for foreign tax)

USA.extras: Federal only, single filer, applied to taxable income after the $16,100 standard deduction. State and local income taxes are extra (0% to about 13%). 3.8% NIIT on investment income above $200k MAGI. 0.9% Additional Medicare tax on wages above $200k.
USA.capital_gains: Long-term: 0/15/20% (single: 0% up to about $49k of taxable income, 20% above about $545k), plus 3.8% NIIT. Short-term: ordinary rates. Home sale exclusion of $250k.
USA.dividends: Qualified dividends: 0/15/20% (+3.8% NIIT). Non-qualified: ordinary rates.

Canada.capital_gains: 50% of the gain is included in income at marginal rates (the planned 2/3 inclusion increase was cancelled). Principal residence is exempt.
Canada.dividends: Eligible dividends are grossed up 38% with a federal and provincial dividend tax credit. The top combined BC rate on eligible dividends is about 36.5%.

United Kingdom.extras: Scottish non-savings, non-dividend income. The £12,570 personal allowance is withdrawn at £1 per £2 above £100k, so the effective marginal rate is about 67.5% between £100k and £125,140. Employee NIC is 8% / 2% (UK-wide).
United Kingdom.capital_gains: UK-wide: 18% (basic) / 24% (higher), annual exempt amount £3,000. Main residence is exempt.
United Kingdom.dividends: UK-wide rates (not Scottish): from April 2026, 10.75% / 35.75% / 39.35%, with a £500 allowance.
United Kingdom.why: The Scottish bands are from gov.uk. The 2026/27 dividend rate rise (+2pp, announced in the Nov 2025 Budget) is from memory and was not verified.

Austria.extras: The 55% band is temporary (in place to 2029). There is no local income tax.
Austria.capital_gains: 27.5% flat on securities and crypto. 30% on real estate (ImmoESt). Main residence is often exempt.

Japan.extras: National tax only. Add a 2.1% reconstruction surtax on the national tax (through 2037), so the top national rate is 45.945%. Add a flat 10% local inhabitant tax on the prior year's income, plus a per-capita levy of about JPY 5,000. Top combined rate is about 55.945%.
Japan.capital_gains: Listed shares: 20.315% separate taxation (15.315% national + 5% local). Real estate: 20.315% if held more than 5 years, 39.63% if 5 years or less.
Japan.dividends: Listed company dividends: 20.315% final (separate taxation option). Alternatively aggregated with a dividend credit.

Thailand.extras: Since 2024, foreign-source income of residents is taxable when remitted to Thailand.
Thailand.capital_gains: Gains on SET-listed shares are exempt for individuals. Other gains are taxed as ordinary income. Real estate sale is subject to withholding on assessed value plus 3.3% specific business tax if held less than 5 years.
Thailand.dividends: 10% final withholding (optional). Alternatively included at progressive rates with a dividend credit.

Portugal.extras: Solidarity surcharge: 2.5% on taxable income from €80k to €250k, and 5% above €250k. IFICI (the 'NHR 2.0' regime): 20% flat for qualifying new residents.
Portugal.capital_gains: Securities: 28% flat, or optional aggregation (with reliefs for long holdings from 2025). Real estate: 50% of the gain is added to progressive income.
Portugal.dividends: 28% flat, or optional aggregation with 50% of the dividend included.

Malaysia.extras: Territorial basis. Foreign-source income remitted by individuals is exempt until 2036 (conditions apply).
Malaysia.capital_gains: No general CGT for individuals (the 2024 CGT applies to companies). RPGT on real property for citizens and PRs: 30% (held up to 3 years), 20% (year 4), 15% (year 5), 0% (year 6 onwards).
Malaysia.dividends: Single-tier dividends are exempt. However, a 2% dividend tax applies on dividends above RM100k a year from YA2025.

Italy.extras: National IRPEF only. Add a regional surcharge of about 1.23% to 3.33% and a municipal surcharge of 0% to 0.9%, so the top marginal rate is about 47%. The middle rate was cut from 35% to 33% by the 2026 Budget.
Italy.capital_gains: 26% substitute tax on financial assets (12.5% on government bonds). Real estate: gains on property held more than 5 years are exempt; otherwise IRPEF, or a 26% substitute tax.

Spain.extras: These bands are state + standard regional combined (each half). Actual regional scales vary: the top combined rate is about 45% in Madrid and 50% to 54% in Valencia and Catalonia.
Spain.capital_gains: Savings scale: 19% (to €6k), 21% (to €50k), 23% (to €200k), 27% (to €300k), 30% above. Same for real estate.
Spain.why: The bands are the standard combined scale. The real combined rate depends on the autonomous community.

Greece.extras: General scale under Law 5246/2025. Lower scales apply for taxpayers with children or under 30. Rental income has its own scale (15/25/35/45%). The solidarity contribution is abolished. Non-dom regime: €100k lump sum.
Greece.capital_gains: 15% on securities (listed holdings under 0.5% are exempt). Real estate CGT of 15% is suspended through 2026.

Cyprus.extras: GHS (health) contribution of 2.65% on income, including dividends, capped at €180k. Non-doms are exempt from SDC for 17 years.
Cyprus.capital_gains: 20% CGT only on Cyprus immovable property (and shares in companies holding it). Securities gains are exempt.
Cyprus.dividends: Special Defence Contribution of 5% (17% before 2026) for domiciled residents, in place of income tax. 0% for non-doms.

New Zealand.extras: ACC earners' levy of about 1.75% on earnings (capped). Foreign investment fund (FIF) regime: 5% deemed return on offshore portfolios above NZD 50k.
New Zealand.capital_gains: No general CGT. The bright-line test taxes residential property sold within 2 years at marginal rates.
New Zealand.dividends: Taxed at marginal rates with imputation credits (28% company credit).

Australia.extras: Medicare levy of 2%. Medicare levy surcharge of 1% to 1.5% for higher earners without private hospital cover. The 2025-26 lowest rate was 16%.
Australia.capital_gains: Taxed at marginal rates with a 50% discount for assets held more than 12 months. Main residence is exempt.
Australia.dividends: Taxed at marginal rates with franking credits (refundable).

France.extras: Thresholds are per household part (quotient familial). High-income surtax (CEHR): 3% above €250k single, 4% above €500k. CDHR: a minimum effective rate of 20% above €250k. Social charges of 9.7% on earned income (CSG/CRDS), partly deductible.
France.capital_gains: PFU flat tax of 31.4% (12.8% income tax + 18.6% social charges). Real estate: 19% + 17.2% social charges, with holding-period taper (exempt after 22 / 30 years). Main home is exempt.
France.dividends: PFU of 31.4% from 2026, or optional progressive scale with a 40% allowance plus social charges.

Germany.extras: The 14% to 42% zone is a linear-progressive formula, not a flat band. Solidarity surcharge: 5.5% of income tax, only above about €20k of tax (taxable income of about €73k+ single), with full rate from about €105k. Church tax: 8% to 9% of income tax if a member.
Germany.capital_gains: Securities: Abgeltungsteuer 25% + soli = 26.375% (+ church tax), with a €1,000 saver allowance. Real estate: exempt after 10 years (or if owner-occupied); otherwise marginal rates.
Germany.why: The PwC page shows 2025 figures (€12,096 / €68,430). The 2026 figures (€12,348 / €69,879) come from German tax press found by search. The 14-42% zone is a smooth formula; the calculator treats it as steps, so it under-states tax for incomes between ~€12k and ~€70k.

Chile.extras: Impuesto Global Complementario. In UTA: exempt to 13.5, then 30, 50, 70, 90, 120, 310. The same factors apply monthly (in UTM) for the employment tax.
Chile.capital_gains: Generally taxed in IGC. Gains on listed shares meeting market-presence rules: 10% sole tax (since 2023). Housing gains: exempt up to 8,000 UF lifetime.
Chile.dividends: Included in IGC with a credit for corporate tax (partial integration, generally 65% of the credit is usable).
Chile.why: The source is a secondary site, not SII (its arithmetic checks against the UTA). The capital gains and dividend notes are from memory.

Indonesia.extras: Personal relief (PTKP) of IDR 54m for a single filer, deducted before the bands.
Indonesia.capital_gains: Listed share sales: 0.1% final tax on gross proceeds. Land and building transfers: 2.5% final tax on gross value. Other gains: progressive rates.
Indonesia.dividends: 10% final tax. Exempt if reinvested in Indonesia (conditions apply).

Philippines.extras: Self-employed people with gross income of PHP 3m or less may opt for an 8% gross tax.
Philippines.capital_gains: Unlisted shares: 15% on net gain. Listed shares: stock transaction tax on gross (0.6%, reduced to 0.1% under CMEPA from Jul 2025). Real property: 6% of the higher of price or FMV.
Philippines.dividends: Dividends from domestic corporations: 10% final tax for residents.
Philippines.why: The capital gains and dividend figures are from memory; the PwC page I read did not cover them.

Mexico.extras: Annual table, applied as fixed fee + marginal rate. States levy payroll taxes on employers, not on individuals.
Mexico.capital_gains: Shares on the Mexican stock exchange: 10% on gain. Real estate and other gains: progressive rates (with averaging). Main home exempt up to a UDI cap.
Mexico.dividends: Additional 10% withholding on dividends from post-2014 profits. Dividends are also aggregated with a corporate tax credit.

Costa Rica.extras: This is the annual scale for self-employed and business income. Employees use a separate monthly salary scale (0/10/15/20/25%). Territorial system: foreign income is generally not taxed.
Costa Rica.capital_gains: 15% on capital gains (Law 9635). For assets held before 2019, an option of 2.25% of gross price.
Costa Rica.why: The employment monthly scale was not verified. The capital gains figures are from memory.

Panama.extras: Territorial system: foreign-source income is not taxed.
Panama.capital_gains: Real estate: 10% on gain (3% of sale price paid in advance). Shares: 10% on gain (5% of price withheld).
Panama.dividends: 10% withholding on nominative shares from Panama-source profits. 5% on foreign-source or certain zone profits.
Panama.why: The capital gains and dividend figures are from memory; the PwC page did not cover them.

Georgia.extras: Flat rate. Territorial system: foreign-source income of individuals is exempt. Small-business status: 1% on turnover up to GEL 500k. Pension contribution of 2% for employees.
Georgia.capital_gains: 20% generally. Property held more than 2 years and certain securities are exempt.
Georgia.why: The capital gains and dividend figures are from memory.

Romania.extras: Flat rate. Employee social contributions are significant: CAS 25% (pension) + CASS 10% (health). CASS of 10% also applies on investment income above minimum-wage-based thresholds.
Romania.capital_gains: Securities via Romanian brokers: 3% (held 1 year or more) / 6% (less than 1 year). Otherwise 16%. Real estate: a transfer tax of 3% or 6% of value, depending on the value threshold.
Romania.why: The capital gains and dividend changes under Law 141/2025 are from memory; the PwC page I read did not state them.

Bulgaria.extras: Flat rate. Bulgaria adopted the euro on 1 Jan 2026. Employee social security is about 13.78% (capped).
Bulgaria.capital_gains: 10%. Gains on shares traded on EU/EEA regulated markets are exempt. Sale of one home, or property held more than 5 years, has exemptions.
Bulgaria.why: The dividend and capital gains rates are from memory; the page did not specify them.

UAE.extras: No personal income tax. 9% corporate tax applies to individuals' business turnover above AED 1m (personal investment and real estate income are excluded).

Malta.extras: Single-rate scale. Residents who are not domiciled are taxed on a remittance basis, with a €5k minimum tax. Social security of about 10% (capped).
Malta.capital_gains: Malta property: final tax of 8% on transfer value (10% if acquired before 2004; 5% for disposals within 5 years in some cases). Securities: gains are taxed at progressive rates, but listed securities are generally exempt.
Malta.dividends: Full imputation: tax credit for 35% corporate tax, so usually no extra tax at top rate. 15% final option on certain investment income.
Malta.why: The capital gains and dividend notes are from memory.

Ireland.extras: Single person; tax credits of about €4k are ignored. USC (approximate): 0.5% to €12,012, 2% to about €28.7k, 3% to €70,044, 8% above (11% on self-employed income above €100k). PRSI of 4.2% (4.35% from Oct 2026). Top marginal rate on employment income is about 52%.
Ireland.capital_gains: 33% (€1,270 annual exemption). Exit tax of 41% (38% from 2026) on funds and ETFs.
Ireland.dividends: Taxed at marginal rates + USC + PRSI (up to about 52%)
Ireland.why: Only the 20%/40% band and the €44k figure were verified. The USC, PRSI and exit tax figures are from memory.

Uruguay.extras: IRPF on labour income. Thresholds are set in BPC (7/10/15/30/50/75/115 times 12 BPC) and indexed each year, so 2026 thresholds are a few percent higher. New residents can elect a 10- or 11-year holiday on foreign capital income.
Uruguay.capital_gains: 12% (often on a deemed basis, e.g. 20% of price, giving an effective 2.4%). Real estate is the same.
Uruguay.dividends: 7% on Uruguayan dividends. 12% on foreign dividends (if no holiday applies).
Uruguay.why: The bands are 2025 values; 2026 BPC indexation was not verified. The 7% dividend rate is from memory; PwC only states 12% for capital income.
